Subject: Mapping SOC 2 scope to deployment modes — Finexa request

Hi Priya,

We're preparing our vendor SOC 2 review for the upcoming procurement board and need to confirm how Redwood's Type II report maps to the different hosting/deployment options. Specifically: 

- Does your SOC 2 Type II (audit period: Apr 1 2025 — Mar 31 2026) explicitly cover Hosted API endpoints, Dedicated GPU pools, and Private/VPC/on-prem installations?
- For Dedicated pools that have burst-to-hosted behavior, do you treat burst capacity as covered by the same report or do you provide a separate bridge letter?
- For Private/VPC and on-prem, what evidence do you provide (if any) when control ownership is split between Redwood and the customer — e.g., KMS keys, network controls, and tenant isolation?

We need a short write-up we can share with our auditors and a copy of the Type II report / any bridge letters. Can you also confirm the sampling window and whether logs/audit trails for token-level activity are included in scope?

Appreciate a quick triage — our vendor review deadline is Jun 4.

Thanks,
Alice Monroe
Senior Information Security Manager
Finexa

--
Finexa Infosec
security@finexa.com

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Monroe <security@finexa.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mapping SOC 2 scope to deployment modes — Finexa request

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Quick triage from our side so you can pass a succinct summary to auditors: 

- Hosted API: INCLUDED in Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report for the audit period you cited (Apr 1, 2025 — Mar 31, 2026). Controls over compute, runtime, logging, monitoring, and change management are in-scope.
- Dedicated GPU pools: INCLUDED when the pool is Redwood-managed and provisioned as a dedicated offering (our standard Dedicated product). For dedicated customers that rely on Redwood-managed networking and capacity, the same Type II report applies; we provide a bridge letter for documented burst behavior that points to Hosted controls for short-duration overflow.
- Private/VPC / on-prem: TYPICALLY OUT OF SCOPE for the standard Type II report unless the deployment is Redwood-managed (i.e., Redwood operates and retains control over the environment). When control is shared or customer-managed (customer owns KMS, networking), we provide an annotated control-ownership matrix and a signed appendix describing which controls are customer responsibilities.

Next steps we propose:
1) I'll attach the Type II report PDF and our standard bridge-letter template for Dedicated->Hosted bursting.
2) We'll produce an annotated control-ownership matrix that maps each deployment mode to the responsible party (Redwood vs customer).
3) If you need logs for sampling, tell us the time window and the types of artifacts (audit logs, token-level access, change management tickets) and we'll confirm availability.

If that's workable I'll loop in Kar—he can confirm the exact artifacts we can share (redactions applied where necessary). Would you like a short call to run through the matrix?

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Manager, Security & Compliance (Vendor Programs)
Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.ai

Attachments: (will send) Redwood_SOC2_Type_II_2025.pdf, Redwood_bridge_letter_dedicated-burst_2025.pdf

Subject: Re: Mapping SOC 2 scope to deployment modes — Finexa request

Thanks Priya — that outline helps. Two clarifications before we schedule a call: 

1) Dedicated pools with burst: For customers using dedicated pools with occasional overflow to Hosted (short-lived), our auditors want to see an explicit statement that the controls covering Hosted overflow are the same operational controls tested in the Type II report (or the bridge letter if applicable). Will the bridge letter explicitly reference the tested control IDs?

2) KMS / key ownership: We have one proposed architecture where our SA uses Redwood Dedicated but brings an external KMS (customer-managed key). In that mixed-control case, will Redwood still include relevant encryption-in-transit and encryption-at-rest controls in the matrix, and how do you recommend we document the split for our auditor?

Also — for sampling, can you confirm what typical retention windows are for audit logs and whether you can provide 90 days of token/audit logs for a narrow set of endpoints (we'll specify endpoints after the call).

Appreciate it — Alice

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Monroe <security@finexa.com>
Cc: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mapping SOC 2 scope to deployment modes — Finexa request

Hi Alice,

Thanks — answering both points in one place so you have language for your auditors.

1) Dedicated + burst-to-hosted: Our bridge letter (attached) explicitly references the control set exercised during the Type II testing. The bridge letter cites the control IDs and control families (CC1–CC7 / common SOC2 designations we reference internally) and clarifies that short-duration overflow is routed to the same production-hosted runtime covered by the audit. We will add a line referencing the audit sampling window (Apr 1 2025 — Mar 31 2026) so auditors can trace the timeframe.

2) Customer-managed KMS / split ownership: When customers bring their own KMS keys and retain key custody, the encryption-at-rest control is annotated as "customer responsibility" in the control-ownership matrix. Redwood still documents the technical controls that protect data in transit and at rest within our environment, but we mark the specific control activities that require customer action (e.g., key rotation, key access policies) and provide guidance text auditors can use.

3) Logs & retention: Standard audit log retention for the in-scope hosted/dedicated environment is 180 days for system-level audit trails; application-level token access logs are retained for 90 days by default. For vendor reviews we can provide a narrow export (redacted where needed) for a 90-day window for specific endpoints.

Deliverables we'll attach to this thread:
- Redwood_SOC2_Type_II_2025.pdf (full report)
- Redwood_bridge_letter_dedicated-burst_2025.pdf (bridge letter with control refs)
- redwood-control-ownership-matrix-20260518.xlsx (annotated matrix)

If you want, we can also produce a one-page summary specifically formatted for auditors that maps: deployment mode -> in-scope? -> control owner -> evidence type. Happy to schedule a 30-minute call (I have availability Thu 05/21 09:30–11:00 PT).

Regards,
